scope.selection_rule: Only implementations classified pass by validation/gpu_correctness/results/results.json are exposed.
scope.operation_count_note: Triangle counting and dynamic triangle counting share one research problem but are separate runnable operations.

build_once_run_many.execution_model: Compile and link the validated implementations once. Each later query invokes the same binary with an operation, backend, canonical graph JSON, parameters, and optional-output flags.
why: No C++ or CUDA compilation occurs per user query.
The command boundary is stable JSON input and JSON output.
The runtime list command reports which validated backends were compiled into the current binary.
A long-lived service can invoke this binary now and can later call the same C++ library in-process if process startup becomes material.

options.description: CUDA device IDs; current validated paths use the first ID unless their facade states otherwise.
Explicitly permit an undirected projection for an undirected operation.
Omit execution statistics from result JSON.
Write result JSON to a file; use - for stdout.

accepted: a JSON array of vertex IDs
an object with a left_partition array
a JSON array of update objects
an object with an updates array
triangle_updates.batch_semantics: EDTC applies every deletion before every insertion, matching the validated artifact.

auxiliary_input_formats.query_graph: A second canonical_edge_list_v1 JSON graph passed with --query-graph.
auxiliary_input_formats.motif_graph: Each --motif value is a canonical_edge_list_v1 JSON graph; its graph.id becomes motif_id.

operations.validated_profile: Maximal gamma quasi-cliques supported by cuQC; the general problem spec's maximum_size and maximal_only choices are not exposed.

operations.partition_rule: Every graph vertex absent from left_partition belongs to the right partition.

backend_constraints.graphminer: undirected induced motifs of size 3 or 4
backend_constraints.graphset: undirected non-induced motifs of size 3 or 4
backend_constraints.dumato: undirected induced motifs of size 3 or 4

operations.command: graphmine run graph-motifs --graph DATA.json --motif MOTIF.json --backend graphminer --induced --include-instances --pretty

operations.validated_profile: The gMatch adapter supports its validated non-induced structural/label matching profile; general declarative edge/vertex predicates are not exposed.
Directed ordered feed-forward triangle A->B, B->C, A->C with distinct vertices, stable event ordering, integer timestamps, and an inclusive max_time_span window.
Unweighted undirected modularity heuristic. Resolution, weighted mode, CPM, and exact optimality are not exposed by the validated adapters.

spec.name: Maximal Clique Enumeration
spec.problem_statement: Given an undirected graph, enumerate every vertex set that forms a clique and is not a proper subset of another clique.

normalization: Reject directed input unless an explicit undirected projection is requested.
Remove self-loops.
Collapse parallel edges into one undirected edge.

problem_inputs.name: minimum_clique_size
problem_inputs.description: Return only maximal cliques at least this large.

problem_inputs.name: result_limit
problem_inputs.description: Maximum materialized cliques; a finite value permits an incomplete result.

required_outputs.name: cliques
required_outputs.description: Each returned vertex set is a distinct maximal clique meeting the size constraint.

required_outputs.name: returned_count
required_outputs.description: Number of materialized cliques.

required_outputs.name: complete
required_outputs.description: True only if all qualifying maximal cliques were enumerated.

optional_outputs.name: total_count
optional_outputs.description: Total qualifying clique count when enumeration completed or exact count-only continuation was performed.

solution_semantics.objective: Enumerate all inclusion-maximal complete vertex sets satisfying minimum_clique_size.
solution_semantics.exactness: Every materialized set must be exact; complete=true requires exhaustive enumeration.
solution_semantics.duplicate_policy: The same vertex set may appear only once.
solution_semantics.ordering: No clique or vertex ordering is semantically required.

validation_rules: Every pair of distinct vertices in each result has an edge.
No outside vertex is adjacent to every vertex in a returned clique.
For complete=true, results equal a trusted exhaustive oracle on tractable graphs.
edge_cases: An empty graph returns no cliques.
An isolated vertex is a size-one maximal clique when minimum_clique_size <= 1.
A complete graph has exactly one maximal clique containing all vertices.

spec.name: Maximum Clique
spec.problem_statement: Given an undirected graph, find a clique with the largest possible number of vertices.

normalization: Reject directed input unless an explicit undirected projection is requested.
Remove self-loops.
Collapse parallel edges into one undirected edge.

problem_inputs.name: return_all_ties
problem_inputs.description: Return every maximum clique rather than one representative.

problem_inputs.name: known_lower_bound
problem_inputs.description: A valid known lower bound on the optimal clique size.

required_outputs.name: maximum_size
required_outputs.description: Cardinality of the best clique found.

required_outputs.name: cliques
required_outputs.description: One maximum clique, or all tied maximum cliques when requested.

required_outputs.name: optimal
required_outputs.description: Whether maximum_size has been proven globally optimal.

optional_outputs.name: upper_bound
optional_outputs.description: Best certified upper bound when optimal=false.

solution_semantics.objective: Maximize the number of vertices in a complete induced vertex set.
solution_semantics.exactness: An exact completed result must have optimal=true; interrupted solvers may return a feasible clique and certified bound.
solution_semantics.duplicate_policy: Tied maximum cliques must be unique as vertex sets.

validation_rules: Every returned set is a clique.
Every returned clique has maximum_size vertices.
optimal=true is valid only when no larger clique exists.
edge_cases: An empty graph has maximum_size 0 and one empty solution conventionally represented by an empty clique list.
A nonempty edgeless graph has maximum_size 1.
A complete graph's unique maximum clique contains every vertex.

spec.name: k-Clique Counting and Enumeration
spec.problem_statement: Given an undirected graph and integer k, count or enumerate every complete vertex set containing exactly k vertices.

normalization: Reject directed input unless an explicit undirected projection is requested.
Remove self-loops.
Collapse parallel edges into one undirected edge.

problem_inputs.name: k
problem_inputs.description: Required number of vertices in each clique.

problem_inputs.name: mode
problem_inputs.description: Whether to count cliques or materialize their vertex sets.

problem_inputs.name: result_limit
problem_inputs.description: Maximum materialized instances in enumerate mode.

required_outputs.name: count
required_outputs.description: Number of k-cliques found; it is the total only when complete=true.

required_outputs.name: complete
required_outputs.description: Whether the count and enumeration cover all k-cliques.

optional_outputs.name: cliques
optional_outputs.description: Distinct k-cliques when mode=enumerate.

optional_outputs.name: per_vertex_count
optional_outputs.description: Number of k-cliques containing each vertex.

solution_semantics.objective: Count or enumerate all size-k complete vertex sets.
solution_semantics.exactness: complete=true requires an exact exhaustive result.
solution_semantics.duplicate_policy: Each unordered vertex set is counted once.
solution_semantics.ordering: Vertex and result order are irrelevant.

validation_rules: Every enumerated set contains exactly k distinct vertices.
Every vertex pair in each result has an edge.
When complete=true, count matches the number of unique qualifying sets.
edge_cases: If k exceeds the vertex count, count is zero.
For k=2, every unique graph edge is a 2-clique.
A complete n-vertex graph contains n choose k k-cliques.

spec.name: Quasi-Clique Mining
spec.problem_statement: Find vertex subsets whose induced subgraphs satisfy a minimum internal-degree fraction, allowing dense groups that are not complete cliques.

normalization: Reject directed input unless an explicit undirected projection is requested.
Remove self-loops.
Collapse parallel edges into one undirected edge.

problem_inputs.name: gamma
problem_inputs.description: Every selected vertex must have induced degree at least ceil(gamma * (|S|-1)).

problem_inputs.name: minimum_size
problem_inputs.description: Minimum vertices in a returned quasi-clique.

problem_inputs.name: maximum_size
problem_inputs.description: Optional upper bound on result size.

problem_inputs.name: maximal_only
problem_inputs.description: Return only qualifying sets not contained in a larger qualifying set.

required_outputs.name: quasi_cliques
required_outputs.description: Unique vertex sets with size, induced edge count, density, and minimum internal degree.

required_outputs.name: complete
required_outputs.description: Whether every qualifying result was found.

optional_outputs.name: count
optional_outputs.description: Number of qualifying results.

solution_semantics.objective: Enumerate induced vertex sets satisfying the gamma minimum-degree condition and size bounds.
solution_semantics.exactness: All reported sets must satisfy the threshold; complete=true means exhaustive enumeration.

validation_rules: Recompute induced degree for every selected vertex.
Verify size bounds.
When maximal_only=true, no result is contained in a larger qualifying set.
edge_cases: gamma=1 reduces the condition to clique mining.
Disconnected sets normally fail for useful gamma values but connectivity is determined solely by the stated degree condition.
No result is returned when minimum_size exceeds the vertex count.

spec.name: k-Core Decomposition
spec.problem_statement: Assign every vertex its largest k for which it belongs to the maximal induced subgraph whose vertices all have internal degree at least k.

normalization: Reject directed input unless an explicit undirected projection is requested.
Remove self-loops.
Collapse parallel edges into one undirected edge.

problem_inputs.name: requested_k
problem_inputs.description: Optionally materialize the vertices and edges of one k-core in addition to the full decomposition.

required_outputs.name: core_number_by_vertex
required_outputs.description: Largest core order containing each vertex.

required_outputs.name: degeneracy
required_outputs.description: Maximum core number in the graph.

optional_outputs.name: requested_core_vertices
optional_outputs.description: Vertices whose core number is at least requested_k.

optional_outputs.name: requested_core_edges
optional_outputs.description: Edges induced by requested_core_vertices.

optional_outputs.name: peeling_order
optional_outputs.description: A valid order in which vertices were removed.

solution_semantics.objective: Compute the complete core decomposition and graph degeneracy.
solution_semantics.exactness: Core numbers and degeneracy are exact.
solution_semantics.duplicate_policy: Each input vertex has exactly one core number.
solution_semantics.ordering: Peeling order may vary while core numbers remain invariant.

validation_rules: Every vertex assigned core c belongs to the c-core.
No vertex belongs to a core with order greater than its reported core number.
The requested k-core equals vertices with core number at least k.
edge_cases: Isolated vertices have core number zero.
An empty graph has degeneracy zero and an empty map.
Every vertex in a complete n-vertex graph has core number n-1.

spec.name: Maximal Biclique Enumeration
spec.problem_statement: Given a bipartite graph, enumerate complete bipartite subgraphs that cannot be extended by adding a vertex to either side.

normalization: Reject directed input unless an explicit undirected projection is requested.
Remove self-loops and collapse parallel edges.
Reject any edge whose endpoints are in the same declared partition.

problem_inputs.name: left_partition
problem_inputs.description: All vertices belonging to the left side.

problem_inputs.name: right_partition
problem_inputs.description: All vertices belonging to the right side.

problem_inputs.name: minimum_left_size
problem_inputs.description: Minimum selected vertices on the left.

problem_inputs.name: minimum_right_size
problem_inputs.description: Minimum selected vertices on the right.

problem_inputs.name: result_limit
problem_inputs.description: Maximum materialized bicliques.

required_outputs.name: bicliques
required_outputs.description: Distinct objects containing left_vertices and right_vertices.

required_outputs.name: returned_count
required_outputs.description: Number of materialized bicliques.

required_outputs.name: complete
required_outputs.description: Whether every qualifying maximal biclique was enumerated.

optional_outputs.name: total_count
optional_outputs.description: Total qualifying bicliques when known exactly.

solution_semantics.objective: Enumerate all inclusion-maximal pairs (L,R) with every possible cross-partition edge present.
solution_semantics.exactness: Every returned pair must be exact; complete=true requires exhaustive enumeration.
solution_semantics.duplicate_policy: Each pair of unordered vertex sets appears once.
solution_semantics.ordering: Order within or among bicliques is irrelevant.

validation_rules: Partitions are disjoint and cover every endpoint used.
Every left result vertex is adjacent to every right result vertex.
No additional vertex can extend either result side while preserving completeness.
edge_cases: A graph with no cross-partition edges has no nonempty bicliques.
An isolated vertex belongs to no biclique under the nonempty-side convention.
A complete bipartite input has one maximal biclique containing both full partitions.

spec.name: Triangle Counting and Listing
spec.problem_statement: Count all unordered triples of vertices connected by all three possible edges and optionally list the triples or their per-vertex and per-edge participation counts.

normalization: Reject directed input unless an explicit undirected projection is requested.
Remove self-loops.
Collapse parallel edges into one undirected edge.

problem_inputs.name: list_instances
problem_inputs.description: Materialize triangle vertex triples.

problem_inputs.name: include_per_vertex_counts
problem_inputs.description: Return triangle participation per vertex.

problem_inputs.name: include_per_edge_counts
problem_inputs.description: Return triangle support per edge.

problem_inputs.name: result_limit
problem_inputs.description: Maximum listed instances; it does not permit truncating the global count.

required_outputs.name: global_triangle_count
required_outputs.description: Exact number of distinct undirected triangles.

required_outputs.name: instances_complete
required_outputs.description: Whether every triangle instance was listed when listing was requested.

optional_outputs.name: triangles
optional_outputs.description: Unique three-vertex triangle instances.

optional_outputs.name: per_vertex_count
optional_outputs.description: Triangles containing each vertex.

optional_outputs.name: per_edge_count
optional_outputs.description: Triangles containing each edge.

solution_semantics.objective: Count every size-three clique exactly once and materialize requested secondary outputs.
solution_semantics.exactness: The global count and requested participation counts are exact.
solution_semantics.duplicate_policy: Each unordered triple is counted and listed once.

validation_rules: Every listed triple contains three distinct pairwise-adjacent vertices.
The sum of per-vertex counts equals three times the global count.
The sum of per-edge counts equals three times the global count.
edge_cases: Graphs with fewer than three vertices have count zero.
A complete n-vertex graph contains n choose 3 triangles.
Isolated vertices have per-vertex count zero.

spec.name: Graph Motif Counting
spec.problem_statement: Count occurrences of one or more supplied small structural patterns in a directed or undirected graph.

normalization: Remove self-loops unless explicitly present in a future motif extension.
Collapse parallel edges with identical direction into one edge.
Preserve edge direction for directed motifs.

problem_inputs.name: motifs
problem_inputs.constraints: nonempty array of small connected patterns
problem_inputs.description: Motif definitions using the same canonical graph format.

problem_inputs.name: induced
problem_inputs.description: Require each occurrence to contain exactly the motif edges among selected vertices.

problem_inputs.name: occurrence_identity
problem_inputs.description: Controls whether automorphism-equivalent embeddings are counted separately.

problem_inputs.name: list_instances
problem_inputs.description: Materialize matching data-graph vertex mappings.

problem_inputs.name: result_limit_per_motif
problem_inputs.description: Maximum listed instances for each motif; counts remain exhaustive.

required_outputs.name: count_by_motif
required_outputs.description: Exact occurrence count under the selected identity semantics.

required_outputs.name: instances_complete_by_motif
required_outputs.description: Whether every requested instance was materialized.

optional_outputs.name: instances_by_motif
optional_outputs.description: Mappings from motif vertices to data-graph vertices.

optional_outputs.name: per_vertex_participation
optional_outputs.description: Occurrence participation counts.

solution_semantics.objective: Count subgraphs isomorphic to each motif under direction, inducedness, and occurrence-identity settings.
solution_semantics.exactness: Counts are exact; listing may be capped but must disclose completeness.
solution_semantics.duplicate_policy: Occurrences follow occurrence_identity and are otherwise unique.
solution_semantics.ordering: Result ordering is irrelevant; directed edge orientation is significant.

validation_rules: Every instance preserves motif adjacency and direction.
Induced instances contain no additional edges among mapped vertices.
Counts account for motif automorphisms according to occurrence_identity.
edge_cases: A motif larger than the data graph has count zero.
Isomorphic motif definitions may produce identical counts but remain separately identified.
Disconnected motif definitions are rejected in version 1.

spec.name: Subgraph Isomorphism and Pattern Matching
spec.problem_statement: Find injective mappings from the vertices of a query graph to a data graph that preserve required edges, direction, and requested attribute predicates.

normalization: Preserve query and data edge direction.
Preserve parallel-edge identity when predicates distinguish edges.
Do not silently remove self-loops used by the query.

problem_inputs.name: query_graph
problem_inputs.description: Pattern graph expressed using canonical_edge_list_v1.

problem_inputs.name: induced
problem_inputs.description: Require mapped vertices to have no extra data edges beyond query edges.

problem_inputs.name: vertex_predicates
problem_inputs.description: Declarative constraints on mapped vertex type, label, or attributes.

problem_inputs.name: edge_predicates
problem_inputs.description: Declarative constraints on mapped edge type, weight, timestamp, or attributes.

problem_inputs.name: result_limit
problem_inputs.description: Maximum materialized mappings.

required_outputs.name: matches
required_outputs.description: Injective query-to-data vertex mappings.

required_outputs.name: returned_count
required_outputs.description: Number of materialized mappings.

required_outputs.name: complete
required_outputs.description: Whether all qualifying mappings were found.

optional_outputs.name: total_count
optional_outputs.description: Exact number of mappings when known.

solution_semantics.objective: Enumerate all injective mappings satisfying structural, directional, inducedness, and attribute constraints.
solution_semantics.exactness: Every returned mapping is exact; complete=true requires exhaustive matching.
solution_semantics.duplicate_policy: Distinct query-to-data mappings are distinct results, even when query automorphisms map to the same data vertex set.

validation_rules: Mappings are injective.
Every query edge has a matching data edge with correct direction and predicates.
Induced matches contain no prohibited extra mapped edges.
All vertex predicates hold.
edge_cases: A query larger than the data graph has no matches.
An empty query has one empty mapping by convention.
Query automorphisms may yield multiple mappings to one data vertex set.

spec.name: Temporal Motif Mining
spec.problem_statement: Count occurrences of a small ordered edge pattern whose matched events occur in the required order within a bounded time window.

normalization: Normalize all edge timestamps to UTC epoch seconds without changing order.
Preserve parallel temporal events as distinct edge IDs.
Preserve edge direction.
Reject missing or invalid timestamps.

problem_inputs.name: temporal_motif
problem_inputs.description: Small graph pattern whose edges have a required total or partial temporal order.

problem_inputs.name: maximum_duration_seconds
problem_inputs.description: Maximum last-edge minus first-edge time for an occurrence.

problem_inputs.name: allow_equal_timestamps
problem_inputs.description: Whether consecutively ordered motif edges may share a timestamp.

problem_inputs.name: temporal_induced
problem_inputs.description: Reject occurrences with additional participating-vertex events inside the occurrence window.

problem_inputs.name: list_instances
problem_inputs.description: Materialize matched edge-event sequences.

problem_inputs.name: result_limit
problem_inputs.description: Maximum listed instances; the total count remains exhaustive.

required_outputs.name: occurrence_count
required_outputs.description: Exact number of temporal motif occurrences.

required_outputs.name: instances_complete
required_outputs.description: Whether all instances were materialized when listing was requested.

optional_outputs.name: instances
optional_outputs.description: Matched vertices, ordered edge IDs, timestamps, and occurrence duration.

optional_outputs.name: per_vertex_participation
optional_outputs.description: Occurrences involving each data vertex.

solution_semantics.objective: Count structurally valid event sequences satisfying motif order, duration, equality, and temporal-inducedness semantics.
solution_semantics.exactness: The occurrence count is exact; listing may be capped.
solution_semantics.duplicate_policy: A distinct ordered tuple of edge-event IDs is a distinct occurrence.

validation_rules: Each instance preserves motif structure and direction.
Event timestamps satisfy the declared order.
Occurrence duration does not exceed maximum_duration_seconds.
No temporal-inducedness violation exists when enabled.
edge_cases: No events yields count zero.
Equal-timestamp events are rejected from strict order positions unless allowed.
Repeated edges between the same endpoints remain distinct events.

correctness: count agreement with exhaustive temporal matcher

spec.name: Disjoint Community Detection
spec.problem_statement: Partition all graph vertices into nonoverlapping communities that maximize a declared within-community quality function.

normalization: Reject directed input unless an explicit undirected projection is requested.
Remove self-loops unless the selected quality definition explicitly retains them.
Collapse parallel edges by summing weights; use unit weights in unweighted mode.

problem_inputs.name: quality_function
problem_inputs.description: Mathematical quality objective optimized by the partition.

problem_inputs.name: resolution
problem_inputs.description: Resolution parameter controlling the preferred community scale.

problem_inputs.name: weight_mode
problem_inputs.description: Use unit edge values or nonnegative input weights.

problem_inputs.name: solution_quality
problem_inputs.description: Whether global optimality is required or a locally optimized partition is acceptable.

required_outputs.name: community_by_vertex
required_outputs.description: Exactly one community assignment for every input vertex.

required_outputs.name: community_count
required_outputs.description: Number of nonempty communities.

required_outputs.name: quality_score
required_outputs.description: Recomputed selected objective value.

required_outputs.name: optimal
required_outputs.description: Whether global optimality was proven.

optional_outputs.name: community_statistics
optional_outputs.description: Size, internal edge value, boundary edge value, and density.

optional_outputs.name: hierarchy
optional_outputs.description: Intermediate or multilevel partitions when meaningful.

solution_semantics.objective: Maximize the selected partition quality over disjoint, exhaustive vertex assignments.
solution_semantics.exactness: Heuristic mode returns a feasible partition without claiming a global optimum.
solution_semantics.duplicate_policy: Community identifiers are arbitrary; partitions equal up to identifier permutation are equivalent.

validation_rules: Every vertex belongs to exactly one nonempty community.
No unknown vertex appears.
Recomputed quality equals quality_score within declared numeric tolerance.
edge_cases: An empty graph has no communities.
Isolated vertices must still receive exactly one assignment.
Multiple partitions may have the same quality score.

correctness: objective gap when an exact oracle is available

spec.name: Centrality and Influential-Node Mining
spec.problem_statement: Compute a declared centrality score for graph vertices and rank the most structurally influential vertices under that definition.

normalization: Preserve direction when requested by the measure.
Remove self-loops unless the selected centrality definition includes them.
Collapse parallel edges according to the selected weight semantics.

problem_inputs.name: centrality_measure
problem_inputs.description: Mathematical definition used to score vertices.

problem_inputs.name: direction_mode
problem_inputs.description: How directed edges contribute where the measure supports direction.

problem_inputs.name: weight_semantics
problem_inputs.description: Interpret edge weights as ignored, connection strength, or path distance.

problem_inputs.name: top_k
problem_inputs.description: Optionally return only the highest-ranked vertices while retaining score-completeness metadata.

problem_inputs.name: measure_parameters
problem_inputs.description: Definition-level values such as PageRank damping, Katz alpha and beta, normalization, or a restricted source set.

problem_inputs.name: solution_quality
problem_inputs.description: Whether approximation or sampling is permitted for expensive measures.

required_outputs.name: ranked_vertices
required_outputs.description: Vertex ID, score, and rank ordered by descending influence.

required_outputs.name: score_definition
required_outputs.description: Resolved measure, direction, weight, normalization, and parameter semantics.

required_outputs.name: complete
required_outputs.description: Whether every vertex was scored and ranking was not truncated.

optional_outputs.name: converged
optional_outputs.description: Whether an iterative measure met its convergence criterion.

optional_outputs.name: error_or_sampling_bound
optional_outputs.description: Known numerical or statistical bound for approximate scores.

solution_semantics.objective: Score and rank vertices exactly according to the selected centrality definition and resolved parameters.
solution_semantics.exactness: Exactness is measure-specific; iterative and approximate methods must disclose convergence or bounds.
solution_semantics.ordering: Descending score with a stable vertex-ID tie break for reproducibility.

validation_rules: Scores are recomputable from score_definition within numeric tolerance.
Every returned vertex exists in the graph.
Ranks are monotonic by score and ties follow the stated policy.
Weight values satisfy the chosen semantics.
edge_cases: Disconnected graphs require explicitly defined closeness behavior.
Dangling vertices require explicitly defined PageRank redistribution.
Tied scores are permitted.
An empty graph produces an empty ranking.
